contradicts.sot: The hotel occupies 12 floors within a 42-storey tower.
contradicts.model_answer: First-party Four Seasons pages state the hotel occupies 12 floors (numbered floors 5–17, omitting 13) within a 42-storey tower at 757 Market Street, whereas skyscraper databases, trade press, engineering portfolios, and residential MLS/brokerage listings for the same tower (757/765 Market Street) predominantly report 40 physical floors (or 37–39 stories) due to skipped floor numbers.
contradicts.notes: First-party Four Seasons pages (fourseasons.com/sanfrancisco/ and press.fourseasons.com/sanfrancisco/hotel-facts/) match the SoT claim ('12 floors within a 42-storey tower'), with the e-brochure clarifying that the hotel lobby is on floor 5 and rooms are on floors 6–17 (12 physical floors, skipping floor 13). However, skyscraper databases (CTBUH Skyscraper Center, Structurae, SkyscraperPage, SKYDB), hospitality trade press (Hotel Business, HospitalityNet), engineering records (Seismic Design Consultants: 37 stories), and residential real estate portals for the tower's condominium address at 765 Market St (Homes.com, Compass, Houzeo, RubyHome, The Real Deal, Late Checkout, San Francisco Condo Market) report 40 physical stories (or 37–39 stories).

contradicts.sot: MKT Restaurant & Bar has four private dining rooms.
contradicts.model_answer: Current search evidence identifies three distinct physical private dining spaces at MKT: Windows, View and Vista. Trio is a combined configuration of Windows, View and the foyer, not a fourth room.
contradicts.notes: Conflicting search results span first-party and third-party sources. The current Four Seasons private-dining page is titled '3 Private Dining Rooms' and describes Windows, View and Vista; it defines Trio as those spaces combined with the foyer. OpenTable says MKT maintains three rooms, and BusinessClass also reports three. The Four Seasons dining index still says four private dining rooms, creating a first-party inconsistency.
